Entry used at power-on and by RESTORE: jumps to restart_game ($09DC), which resets the stack, the chips and the interrupt vectors and runs module 1 (the engine at $0C00).

Entry the engine and every module call to change module: X is the module's number (0 front end, 1 engine, 3 pole vault, 4 diving, 5 relay, 6 dash, 7 gymnastics, 8 freestyle relay, 9 100 m freestyle, 10 skeet). Loads it unless its file is already in ($09E9), then jumps to its entry.

The NMI handler ($0318 points here): RESTORE on its own returns at once; RESTORE with RUN/STOP held (column 7 of row 7 read through $DC00/$DC01) clears the resume address's high byte at $085E and restarts the game at restart_game, which then goes to the main menu.

Load and unpack module X. Puts the I/O and KERNAL in ($01 = $36), marks a load under way at $085F, takes the file's one-letter name from module_letters ($0AF3,x) into $087E and loads it from drive 8 to its own address through the KERNAL (SETLFS, SETNAM, LOAD), retrying on error. Blanks the screen for A and I. Then copies the packed bytes from mod_src to mod_dst until mod_end, expanding the run-length codes: $BF n is n zeros, $CF n v is n copies of v, any other byte is itself. Clears $085F and returns with X kept.
Store A at the unpacker's destination pointer ($10/$11) and step it on.
Read the next packed byte from the source pointer ($12/$13) and step it on.

Reset everything and start the engine: stack to $FF, init_machine ($0A10), then X = 1. With bit 7 of $083D clear the engine is in memory and its entry is taken at once; with it set (swimming unpacks over the engine) the engine is loaded again first.

Load module X unless it is already there, then jump to it. A load is skipped when no earlier load was cut short ($085F clear) and the letter in $087E is this module's. Then pushes the module's entry minus one, waits for raster line 11, selects video bank 0 ($DD00 = $17) and returns into the module with A = $FF.

Put the machine in a known state: waits for raster line 251, copies the KERNAL's IRQ, BRK and NMI vectors (with NMI = nmi_restore) from $0AED to $0314, sets the processor port ($00 = $2F, $01 = $36), zeroes the sprite, collision and colour registers, the filter and volume, sets the multicolour colours (1 white, 2 red), turns off every CIA interrupt but CIA 1's timer A, sets the keyboard port directions and the background to cyan, and loads each SID voice's seven registers from $0A86. Ends by jumping to the KERNAL's UNTLK at $FFAB, which tells the drive to stop talking and returns to init_machine's caller.
Seven bytes copied into each of the three SID voices by init_machine: frequency 0, pulse width $0800, control 0 (gate off), attack/decay 0 and sustain/release 0.
The low bytes of each module's packed load address, one per module number 0-11 (the file loads there; the unpacker reads from it). The high bytes follow at mod_src_hi.
The high bytes of each module's packed load address: A $8000, B $4000, C $E000, D $8200, E $8300, F $8000 (twice), H $6580, I $6D40 (twice), K $8000, L $4000.
The low bytes of where each module unpacks to; high bytes at mod_dst_hi.
The high bytes of where each module unpacks to: A $4000, B $0C00, C $E000, D $4000, E $5800, F $4000, H $4000, I $1000, K $4000, L $C400.
The low bytes of the address the unpacker stops at for each module; high bytes at mod_end_hi.

The low bytes of each module's entry minus one, pushed for the RTS that enters it; high bytes at mod_entry_hi.

The registration screen's raster interrupt: runs the next of eight handlers in turn, taken from $333A/$3342 and pushed for an RTS, and sets the line of the next. The registration's steps, by $22: 0 start with no players; 1 show the next player's name line; 2 type the name; 3 "PICK YOUR COUNTRY" line; 4 choose the flag; 5 all registered: "IS THIS CORRECT?", and Y restarts the engine ($0900) to carry on with the event

Typing a name: up to ten characters at $0417, DEL to rub one out (with a short pause), RETURN to finish. A name the same as an earlier player's is refused; an empty name ends the registration when there is at least one player
Compares the typed name with each registered player's; on a match it drops its own return address so the RETURN is ignored
